scope: If an initial measure is dominated by K times a reference measure and a measurable map preserves the reference measure on preimages of measurable sets, the transported mass of any measurable target set is at most K times that set's reference measure.
environment: Prepared pinned Lean project at work/lean-verification/independent-source; native macOS arm64 Lean executable.

candidate_theorem_status.interpretation: The measure bound is a kinematic consequence conditional on a smooth volume-preserving flow map; it does not verify that the candidate field satisfies all Navier-Stokes CandidateProperties.

limitations: The Lean theorem assumes measure domination and measure preservation; it does not derive the flow map or its Jacobian equation.
Applying it to a constructed velocity additionally requires a smooth global flow diffeomorphism on each preterminal interval.
The three-dimensional ball ratio (R/a)^3 is the classical Euclidean volume scaling; the theorem itself leaves the target-set volume abstract.
No endpoint flow at t=1, molecular dynamics, collisions, or constitutive-viscosity law is covered.
